newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST - HK newspaper headlines - Jan 20.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - HK newspaper headlines - Jan 20.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- TA KUNG PAO - The China-appointed Preparatory Committee has suggested 20 pieces of Hong Kong legislation be repealed in full or in part because they are judged inconsistent with the territory's Basic Law. Some clauses under the Bill of Rights would be dropped after the handover.

- Beijing has instructed that propaganda units should provide powerful ideological guarantees for reforms, development and stability in the new year, and create a good atmosphere to welcome Hong Kong's return to China.
- MING PAO - A national foreign economic relations conference will be held in Beiijing today to confirm the principle of positively, reasonably and effectively making use of foreign investments.
- Taiwan's business sector is against the government's decision to limit investments on the mainland.

- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- Hongkong Telecom will today accuse the powerful U.S. telecoms regulator, the Federal Communications Commission, of trying to undermine its revenues in a bid to aid U.S. telecom companies.
- Air Macau replaced its Singaporean chief executive with a senior aviation offical from China in a move underlining the growing Chinese dominance of the regional carrier.
- HONGKONG STANDARD - Beijing is set to gradually cut links between state-run enterprises listed on Hong Kong's stock market and central ministries and regional governments.
- Shanghai and Taiwan investors completed negotiations for the first mainland-Taiwan bank.
